aka.mnemonic_text: Picture a person standing under a low horizontal beam, their legs splayed wide into those two trailing strokes at the bottom — they've just sprinted across a scorching desert and their whole sunburned face has flushed a furious, glowing red.

ame.mnemonic_text: Picture a window with a flat roof across the top, and behind the glass four little dashes are frozen mid-fall on either side of the frame — that's the rain you're watching streak down the pane.

ana.mnemonic_text: See that little roof up top with two dots tucked under it? It's the crooked stone entrance to a hillside, and the wide legs below open outward like a mouth in the rock, swallowing the dark inside — you're staring straight into the cave.

ao.mnemonic_text: Picture a garden trellis with a single vine climbing up it, and hanging from that vine is one fat, round moon that's caught the twilight — the whole thing glowing that impossible shade between the sky and the sea, blue-green.

ashi-foot.mnemonic_text: Picture a square kneecap sitting on top, and below it the strokes splay out into a leg that plants down and kicks forward — that little wedge at the bottom is the heel and toes pressing into the ground. The whole shape is one stride caught mid-step: a foot.

bou.mnemonic_text: Picture a single line drawn straight up and down, perfectly vertical with nothing else around it — that's exactly what you'd sketch if someone handed you a plain wooden stick and told you to draw it. One clean line, standing on end: a stick.

chichi.mnemonic_text: See those four strokes crossing at the top like raised arms, with two legs planted wide below? That's your father standing over the barbecue, tongs held high in both hands, proudly announcing dinner is ready.

chikara.mnemonic_text: Picture a flexed arm: the long stroke sweeps down and hooks like a bent elbow, and the short stroke is the muscle bulging out of it. That straining, hooked arm is pure power.

gonben.mnemonic_text: Picture a mouth at the bottom — that little box — stacked with horizontal lines rising off it like speech bubbles floating upward, one on top of another. Every line is another sentence leaving the mouth: this is words spilling out as speech.

haba.mnemonic_text: Picture a hook nailed into the wall, and over that top bar someone has draped a rectangle of fabric so it hangs down in two long folds — the vertical stroke is the drape falling straight to the floor. That limp, hanging shape is a piece of cloth.

hachigashira.mnemonic_text: Picture a single log that someone brought an axe down on: the two strokes are the halves falling apart, leaning away from each other where the blade split them clean down the middle. That fresh split is your marker for eight.

hi-fire.mnemonic_text: Picture a single log standing upright, with two sparks flicking off its sides — that's exactly what 火 looks like. Those sparks jumping into the air tell you the whole thing is on fire.

hi-sun.mnemonic_text: Picture a little window with one bar across the middle — that squat rectangle divided in two is 日, and behind the glass you can see the blazing sun climbing up to start a new day.

hidari.mnemonic_text: Picture a snake coiled up tight inside a closed box, its body looping around with just its head poking up through the top — that little gap at the top of 巳 is the head peeking out. When you lift the lid you find it has already curled itself into that shape: a snake, done and waiting.

hito.mnemonic_text: Picture two legs mid-stride, one planted and one swinging forward, the whole body balanced on that walking gait — those two slanting strokes are a single person striding across the page.

hitoashi.mnemonic_text: Look at 儿 head-on and you're staring at someone standing with their feet planted apart, the two strokes sweeping down and out like a pair of sturdy human legs mid-stride.

hitoyane.mnemonic_text: Picture a little pot: the short dash on top is the tiny knob you grab, and the wide horizontal stroke beneath it is the flat disc resting snugly over the rim. Together they snap down into place as the lid.

ichi.mnemonic_text: Picture a single flat line stretching out in front of you — one long horizon where the flat earth meets the sky. That's the one, level ground you're standing on.

ireru.mnemonic_text: See how 入 is a person leaning forward, one leg swinging ahead of the other as they duck under a low doorway. That forward lean is someone mid-stride about to enter.

ishi.mnemonic_text: See that little box tucked under a leaning cliff-face? That's the mouth of a cave in the hillside, and the boxy shape sitting at its base is a big rounded stone that rolled down and came to rest there — one solid stone.

itohen.mnemonic_text: Picture a spool up top with a single strand spilling off it, and below, three loose fibers splayed out where the strands have frayed apart — that whole tangle is one piece of thread.

itoko.mnemonic_text: Picture a single loop of thread pinched at the top and left dangling, its two loose ends trailing off below — so small and fine you have to squint to see it. That flimsy little dangling loop is your tiny thread.

iwaku.mnemonic_text: Picture a wide-open mouth, that squat outer box, with a single tongue stroke lying flat across the middle — the tongue mid-flap, pushing out a word. That flat tongue in the open mouth is a mouth caught in the act to say something.

juu.mnemonic_text: Picture two matchsticks laid across each other, one lying flat and one standing straight up, crossing at the middle to make a perfect plus sign — the exact mark you scratch on a wall when you've counted all ten fingers on both hands. That little cross is ten.

kai-shell.mnemonic_text: See the boxy top as a clam's ridged shell, and the two little legs at the bottom as it tips open — and out spill the coins, because in old Japan these shells were the money.

kakeru.mnemonic_text: Picture a person slouched sideways in a chair, their body bent into that leaning top stroke while their legs sprawl out below — mouth cracked wide open in a huge, jaw-stretching yawn, so worn out they lack the energy to sit up straight.

kanehen.mnemonic_text: Picture a little roof at the top, and underneath it two tiny nuggets sitting on a stand — this is the covered vault where you pile up your gold.

kawa.mnemonic_text: Look at 川 and you're standing on a bank watching three long streams of water pour down the page side by side, the outer two bending with the current. Those three vertical channels flowing together are a river.

keigamae.mnemonic_text: Picture two tall walls dropping straight down from a flat roof, open at the bottom like a doorway with no floor. Tip it upright in your mind and those three sides are the front, top, and back of a wide box sitting open toward you.

ki.mnemonic_text: See that vertical stroke as a trunk, the horizontal line as a branch spreading out, and the two legs sweeping down as roots gripping the soil — it's a tree standing right there in front of you.

ko.mnemonic_text: See that top stroke swinging out like two little arms thrown wide, resting on a body wrapped snugly in a blanket that trails to a single point below? That's a bundled-up child, arms open, running to you.

kokorohen.mnemonic_text: Picture a tall candle standing upright, with a tiny flame flickering off each side of the wick — that thin vertical stroke and its two little side dashes. This candle is the one you light when you're pouring your whole heart into a wish, so 忄is the heart, squeezed slim and standing off to the left.

kome.mnemonic_text: Picture a single grain in the middle with husks flying off in every direction — the top strokes spraying up, the bottom strokes kicking down — like a kernel bursting apart the instant it's threshed. That little explosion of scattering pieces is a grain of rice.

koromo.mnemonic_text: See that little cross-stroke on top as a coat hanger's hook, and the wide, splayed strokes hanging below it as the sleeves and hem draping down — the whole shape is a shirt hung up to dry, a piece of clothing.

kougatsu.mnemonic_text: Picture a steel I-beam standing between two flat concrete slabs: the top and bottom strokes are the slabs, the line down the middle is the beam being lowered into place. That single girder holding the whole thing up is the heart of any construction site.

kuchi.mnemonic_text: Look at that perfect little square — it's a wide-open mouth caught mid-yawn, the four straight strokes framing the gaping hole. That squared-off gap is exactly what it means: a mouth.

kunigamae.mnemonic_text: Picture four solid walls drawn as one unbroken square with no door and no window — you walk all the way around and there's no way out. That closed box of walls is an enclosure.

kuro.mnemonic_text: Picture an old cast-iron stove: the grid at the top is the fuel packed inside, and the four dots along the bottom are the flames licking up underneath it. Burn it long enough and the whole thing is caked in soot — that's why this shape means black.

kuruma.mnemonic_text: Look at 車 straight on: the box in the middle is the body of a cart, the line spearing down through it is the axle running end to end, and the two horizontal bars are the wheels sticking out on either side. It's a wooden cart drawn from above — the original vehicle.

kusakanmuri.mnemonic_text: See those two little humps with the line slicing across them? That's two clumps of grass poking up out of the ground, and the horizontal stroke is the soil they're sprouting from — a fresh patch of grass.

mannaka.mnemonic_text: Picture a wooden shield with one long vertical plank down the middle and two crossbars nailed across it — that's 干, the flat board a warrior holds up. It's been left out in the sun so long that it's cracked and completely dry.

me.mnemonic_text: Look at 目 straight on and it's an eye stood on its end: the outer box is the eyelid framing everything, and the two lines inside are the pupil pinched between them, staring right back at you. That vertical eye is exactly what it means — eye.

mimi.mnemonic_text: Look at 耳 sideways and you're staring at the side of someone's head: that tall outer frame is the ear's outer rim, and the stack of horizontal lines inside are the ridges and folds curving down into the canal. It's a whole ear stood up on the page.

miru.mnemonic_text: Look at the top box of 見 as a big single eye, and the two strokes underneath are the wobbly legs it walks around on — an eyeball on legs that wanders your room, stopping to see everything it can.

mizu.mnemonic_text: Look at 水 and you'll see a single central stream running straight down, with two smaller trickles splashing off to either side — it's the exact moment a drop hits the surface and sprays outward. That splash frozen mid-air is water.

mongamae.mnemonic_text: Look at 門 head-on: two tall pillars framing the left and right, each topped with a little swinging panel, and you can practically hear them creak as they open. Those two heavy doors standing side by side are the entrance to a walled courtyard — a gate.

mushi.mnemonic_text: Look at 虫: that fat box with the vertical line through it is a plump body skewered on a pin, and the little stroke flicking off the bottom right is a leg twitching — a single insect mounted in a collector's display case.

nagai.mnemonic_text: Picture an old wizard standing tall, his flowing beard streaming down from his chin in a wide fan of strokes that pool at the bottom. That beard has been growing untouched for decades — impossibly, endlessly long.

ni.mnemonic_text: Picture two chopsticks laid flat on the table, one resting just above the other, waiting for your meal. Two parallel lines, two chopsticks — that's two.

nikuduki.mnemonic_text: Picture a butcher's frame, and hanging inside it are two thick slabs strung up side by side on hooks — those are the two little person-shapes tucked under the roof of 肉. It's a window into the shop where the meat hangs.

ninben.mnemonic_text: See those two strokes leaning together — a tall body with one leg striding forward, forever caught mid-step on the left edge of the kanji. That's a person walking, always shoved over to the left side to make room for the rest of the character.

onna.mnemonic_text: Picture a dancer caught mid-move: one leg swung out and crossing over the other, arms flung wide across her body. Those sweeping crossed strokes are a woman frozen in the middle of her dance.

oozato.mnemonic_text: Picture a stack of little rooftops piled up on the right side of the page, each one a bump curving down into the long pole of the road that runs past them — that huddle of houses along the road is a village.

rekka.mnemonic_text: Those four little dots are the glowing embers left at the bottom of a campfire pit, each one a tiny tongue of flame licking up from underneath — the fire burning along the bottom.

san.mnemonic_text: Picture three thin pancakes stacked flat on a plate, one on top of another with a little gap between each — that's exactly the three horizontal lines of 三, so every time you see it, you're literally counting three.

sanzui.mnemonic_text: See those three little strokes stacked down the left side? They're three droplets flicking off a wet paintbrush, one after another, splashing down into a puddle of water.

shimesu.mnemonic_text: See that flat top line? That's the tabletop of a stone altar, resting on a single strong pillar, with two carved legs splaying out at the base to hold it steady. On its surface you set your offering out for everyone to show — a proper altar.

shinnyou.mnemonic_text: See how the bottom stroke sweeps out flat and long with a little kick at the end? That's a winding road stretching away from you, and the two strokes above it are your own footsteps stepping onto it as you advance forward.

shiro.mnemonic_text: Picture a single drop of milk with a tiny slanted spark of light flicking off its top: that little stroke sitting above the boxy shape is the glint on the drop as it catches the sun. The whole thing is one bright bead of the whitest white you've ever seen.

shita.mnemonic_text: Picture a mouth flap at the bottom with a little cross sticking up out of it — that's a slab of meat lifting a flag as it pushes its way out past your teeth. That thing wagging out of the mouth is your tongue.

shou.mnemonic_text: Picture a single tiny seed in the center, with two little hands pinching in from either side to show off just how small it is. Those pinching fingers around the speck are 小 — small.

sun.mnemonic_text: Picture a carpenter's flat wooden ruler lying down, with a single tick mark dropping off its right edge — that little notch is where the thumb pins it in place to measure off exactly one inch.

ta.mnemonic_text: Look at 田 from above and you're a farmer standing at the edge of your land: two lines cross in the middle like the narrow dirt paths you walk between the plots, chopping the big square into four neat green squares. That grid of squares is your flooded rice field.

takai.mnemonic_text: Look at 高 from top to bottom: a little roof, then a window box, then another wider room stacked underneath — a slender tower building rising floor by floor into the sky. Every stroke is just one more story added, until the whole thing stands impossibly tall.

takekanmuri.mnemonic_text: See those two identical halves standing side by side, each with a short stroke slanting off and a long stroke dropping straight down? Those are two tall stalks with their leaves flicking out — a little grove of bamboo.

tatsu.mnemonic_text: Picture a person planted on a wide flat platform: that top dot is their head, the two little strokes underneath are arms thrown out for balance, and the long bottom line is the solid ground pressing back against their feet — you're watching someone stand.

te.mnemonic_text: Picture a wrist at the bottom with the long vertical stroke running up through the palm, while the three horizontal strokes fan out sideways like fingers spread wide — you're looking straight at an open hand.

tehen.mnemonic_text: Picture a vertical arm with three little strokes branching off the side — that's the thumb and fingers curling out. It's a hand reaching in from the left edge of the kanji to grab hold of whatever comes next.

ten.mnemonic_text: See that tiny slanted mark 丶 — it's a single droplet of water frozen mid-fall, caught the instant it slid off the tip of a leaf. That one little stroke is a drop.

tomeru.mnemonic_text: Picture a single foot planted flat on the ground, that low horizontal stroke being the sole, with the upright and the little side-stem poking up like the toes and heel dug in. The foot refuses to take one more step — it's frozen mid-stride to stop.

tsuchi.mnemonic_text: Picture a wooden signpost hammered into the ground, its post crossed by one board, and the long horizontal line at the bottom is the flat earth it's planted in — a marker standing in the soil, staking out a patch of earth.

tsuki.mnemonic_text: See how 月 is a tall window with two bars across the middle? Picture yourself pressing your face to that narrow window at night, and framed perfectly inside it hangs the crescent moon.

uma.mnemonic_text: Look at 馬 side-on: the top box is the head, and those four little legs dashing along the bottom are hooves kicking up dust. Picture that boxy body galloping past you and you're looking at a horse.

ushi.mnemonic_text: See that top stroke slanting off to the side? That's the single horn tilting on the head, and the two crossbars below are the sturdy shoulders and back of the animal standing under it — you're looking straight at a cow.

yamahen.mnemonic_text: Look at 山 straight on: three peaks pushing up from one flat ground line, the tall one in the middle flanked by two shorter shoulders. That's the exact jagged silhouette of a mountain against the sky.

yumi.mnemonic_text: Look at 弓 side-on: those stacked curves are a strip of springy wood bent back on itself, notched top and bottom where the string would hook. Pull it taut and you're holding a bow.
